conventions.convention: Dimension d is a positive integer. A van Hove sequence consists of bounded Lebesgue-measurable regions of positive volume tending to infinity, with every fixed-width two-sided Euclidean boundary layer having negligible relative volume.

The potential is even and Borel measurable with values in R ∪ {+∞}. Stability concerns every finite simple configuration. Superstability means a stable part plus an everywhere nonnegative part bounded below by a positive constant on a maximum-norm neighborhood of zero. A divergent positive core is a separate stronger condition.

Regularity uses a nonnegative nonincreasing integrable maximum-norm envelope, bounding the negative part globally and both signs sufficiently far away. Canonical sectors use labelled positional Lebesgue integrals divided by N!, with vacuum partition 1 and collision integrand zero.

Periodic energy includes nontrivial images of the same particle and excludes only the identical point. A positive infinite pair term makes the energy +∞. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson partition is e^(−volume) times the 1/N!-normalized grand partition.

The empirical field averages translations of the periodic continuation over one fundamental cube. It describes a uniformly sampled spatial location, rather than the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin.

Exact canonical limits are asserted at positive interior attainable densities. The duality theorem assigns endpoint values by the upper-semicontinuous concave extension; this does not assert positive finite-volume endpoint partitions.
At beta zero the weight is z^N times hard admissibility, retaining every forbidden periodic-image pair. No value is assigned to 0·(+∞).

The controlled shell has exact particle number and a diagonally selected shrinking positional energy-density window. Neither arbitrary prescribed shrinking widths nor an exact-energy surface measure is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, HB, superstability, regularity, and z,beta > 0, free and periodic normalized-Poisson pressure limits agree and equal −min_P{I(P)+beta Phi(P)−rho(P) log z}; the minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology.

For a stable regular potential and beta > 0, every sequence L_j → ∞, N_j/L_j^d → rho has normalized canonical logarithm tending to F(rho), whenever rho > 0 lies in the interior of the effective domain of the concave envelope defined in the Statement.

For the decreasing integrable tail, eta(g) → 0, the displayed lattice-shell sum is bounded by 2^(d−1)g^(−d)eta(g), and gaps can be selected with g(ell) → ∞, g(ell)/ell → 0, and (ell/g(ell))^d eta(g(ell)) → 0.
P(alpha,beta)=sup_{rho≥0}(F_beta(rho)+alpha rho), and F_beta(rho)=inf_alpha(P(alpha,beta)−alpha rho) on the closed effective domain, with the specified endpoint extension.
For the stated superstable splitting, there are A > 0 and B ≥ 0 such that every finite configuration satisfies H_phi(omega) ≥ A sum_i N_Ci(omega)^2 − B N(omega).

Assuming the exact-N rate equals F_beta(rho) at an interior density and z is supporting, canonical empirical fields have a strictly negative exponential rate outside every open local-tame neighborhood of the grand minimizer set; a singleton gives convergence in probability.

Torus-invariant laws with uniformly bounded finite-volume entropy densities have relatively sequentially compact periodically continued laws, uniformly integrable local counts, and limit entropy bounded by the entropy-density liminf. Empirical-field convergence in probability to P_* transfers to local-tame convergence of the continued laws.

concerns.concern: The Definition introduces the barycenter formula 'For a probability law C_L on finite configurations' and states it for every local tame f, without assuming E_C_L N < ∞. The displayed signed integrals need not exist. For d=L=1, take configurations with N=n and probabilities proportional to n^(−2), and f(omega)=(−1)^{N_[0,1)(omega)}N_[0,1)(omega). Every translated periodic configuration has exactly n points in [0,1), so R_L,omega(f)=(−1)^n n; both positive and negative barycenter integrals are infinite. The probability-mixture measure exists, but its claimed tame expectation formula is undefined on this stated domain. The subsequent stationarity/intensity lemma correctly imposes finite expected N.

The Statement assigns ordinary probabilities to the inverse image of every open tau_L neighborhood U, and step 1.2 invokes the cited LDP on U^c without a measurability qualification. The source distinguishes the evaluation sigma-algebra from the much finer local-tame topology: Georgii 1994, printed p.172, defines empirical-field measurability for the evaluation sigma-algebra; Theorem 2, printed p.175, requires a measurable functional and explicitly specializes to a measurable set. Arbitrary tau_L-open sets need not be evaluation-measurable. For example, bounded local indicators detecting an exact pair displacement distinguish a continuum of periodically repeated two-point patterns; arbitrary unions of their expectation-open sets can encode nonmeasurable sets of displacement parameters. Thus coordinatewise measurability does not justify these probabilities. Specify measurable neighborhoods or establish an outer-probability formulation. The same qualification must be checked in fixed-N equivalence, periodic fixed-N equivalence, periodic-law transfer and the controlled-shell conclusions.

Steps 3.1 and 5.1 apply the Poisson empirical-field upper bound to topologically closed sets K and K ∩ U^c, with U any open tau_L neighborhood, but do not establish evaluation measurability or use outer probabilities. The cited Georgii–Zessin framework equips law space with an evaluation sigma-algebra separately from its local topology and requires measurable empirical functionals. The event A_L itself is measurable; the auxiliary arbitrary-neighborhood events are the unsupported part. This is the same measurability issue as in the canonical-conditioning lemma, occurring here in an independent Poisson-LDP argument.

seams_checked.note: The earlier supplier covers stable power-tempered free-cube grand pressure. This batch proves the broader decreasing-integrable-tail result locally and does not attribute canonical or arbitrary-boundary conclusions to the earlier theorem.

The page identifies this prerequisite as convex-contact and calibration context. Its actual ensemble arguments use the separately identified finite-dimensional separation and biconjugation suppliers, without importing physical contact assumptions.

The earlier regular-shell interface concerns regular phase-space levels and weighted surface measures. This batch explicitly distinguishes its positional energy-density windows and proves their selection separately.

The configuration, Poisson-reference, entropy, local-tame, compactness and spatial-information interfaces retain their finite-intensity, standard-Borel and choice hypotheses. The arbitrary-open-set probability concerns are additional obligations in this batch, rather than conclusions supplied by the entropy page.

The inspected physical consumers retain numerical energy conversion, positional scope, interior density, supporting activity, uniqueness, differentiability, boundary and stronger-core conditions. They explicitly add entropy-controlled periodic-law transfer when passing from empirical fields to expectations of local tame observables, and retain the mathematical suppliers' draft conditional status.
